awd_abstract_narration:
This award will support U.S.-based researchers to participate in the conference “Beyond Uniform Hyperbolicity” (BUH), to take place at the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste, Italy, from June 2 to June 13, 2025. This conference, the eleventh in a long-standing series held every 2–3 years since 2001, has been hosted in various locations worldwide, including twice in the United States. The main theme of the event is dynamics, a subfield of pure mathematics that models complex phenomena -- such as the motion of gas molecules in confined spaces, weather patterns, and planetary motion -- and provides critical theoretical insights into a range of scientific fields. Building on its successful history of advancing knowledge, BUH 2025 will offer a valuable opportunity for emerging researchers to engage with leading experts, explore current research topics, and forge new collaborations. The conference format, featuring six mini-courses and a selection of stand-alone talks, has proven highly effective for advanced learning. Moreover, the welcoming environment of ICTP will foster meaningful interactions between researchers of all backgrounds and experience levels. The conference websites are: https://indico.ictp.it/event/10841 (first week), https://indico.ictp.it/event/10935 (second week).
 
This conference focuses on the most significant advancements in the study of dynamical systems exhibiting various forms of hyperbolicity. The topics covered by BUH 2025 will include: weak hyperbolicity (partial hyperbolicity, nonuniform hyperbolicity, singular hyperbolicity, positive Lyapunov exponent); random dynamics and stationary measures; physical (Sinai-Ruelle-Bowen and u-Gibbs) measures; statistical properties (decay of correlations, limit theorems, speed of mixing); entropy theory and coding for dynamics with hyperbolicity; holomorphic dynamics and hyperbolicity; group actions and smooth rigidity.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Dynamics is a subarea of Mathematics that studies quantitative and qualitative aspects of the time evolution of systems governed by deterministic laws. The classical examples of such systems come from celestial mechanics, but the theory applies to situations originating from all kinds of natural systems, as well as purely theoretical models. 

It was discovered in the last century that deterministic dynamics can emulate random behavior. This phenomenon is popularly known as "chaos". The prototypical type of chaotic dynamical systems are called "uniformly hyperbolic". However, such idealized systems do not reflect the full complexity of chaotic dynamical behavior; therefore the need to explore more complex situations. 

Since 2001, the conferences "Beyond Uniform Hyperbolicity" aim to bring together people doing cutting-edge research in chaotic dynamics. The eleventh edition of the conference took place in the International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste, Italy from 2nd to 13th of June, 2025.  More than 200 people from numerous countries participated. The scientific program featured 6 minicourses, 18 plenary talks, 18 parallel talks, and 11 lightning talks by graduate students.

The National Science Foundation grant DMS-2505218 provided $40,000 which supported 20 participants, 12 of whom graduate students, affiliated with 14 different universities across the United States.  Notably, approximately 40% of the U.S.-based participants received funding through the grant. This support from the NSF was instrumental in enabling graduate students and early-career mathematicians to take part in this valuable formative experience.
